exposure: Intrathecal bupivacaine (10 mg) plus midazolam (2 mg)
outcome: Duration of analgesia (time to first analgesic request)
Total analgesic consumption within 24 hours postoperatively
cohort: 100 patients scheduled for elective lower segment cesarean section (LSCS).
finding: The addition of intrathecal midazolam to bupivacaine significantly enhanced postoperative analgesia in patients undergoing LSCS, providing prolonged pain relief, lower VAS scores, reduced analgesic consumption, and comparable safety.
mod_finding: The study found improved postoperative pain management for patients undergoing lower segment cesarean section (LSCS) with the addition of intrathecal midazolam.
